overview.description: Brisca is the Spanish counterpart of Italian Briscolaâ€”a point-trick game played with the 40-card Spanish deck without suit-following obligation. Card ranking: Ace (11pts) > 3 (10pts) > King (4pts) > Queen (3pts) > Jack (2pts) > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 2 (0pts). The trump suit is determined by a face-up card beside the stock pile. Each trick won adds to the player's score pile; the winner is first to 61 points.

history.origins: Brisca is the Spanish adaptation of the Italian Briscola, sharing the same unusual card ranking (Ace > Three > picture cards). It spread throughout the Iberian Peninsula and Latin America.
timeline: 1600s-1700s: Briscola-type games cross from Italy into Spain.
1800s: Brisca standardized as a household and tavern game in Spain.
Present: A Spanish national game alongside Mus and Tute; widely played in Spain and Spanish-speaking Latin America.
history.evolution: Brisca is virtually identical to Italian Briscola. The main differences: Spanish use of the 40-card baraja espaÃ±ola deck; the 7 of trump (called the 'Siete de Velo' or 'Manilla' in some regions) has elevated importance in some regional variants. Portuguese Bisca uses the 7 of trump as the second-highest card.
history.cultural: A deep part of Spanish cafÃ© and park culture. Spain's 'big three' card games are traditionally Mus, Tute, and Brisca.

setup.deck: 40-card Spanish deck (baraja espaÃ±ola). OR: French 52-card deck stripped of 8s, 9s, 10s.
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards each. Turn one card face-up beside stock to indicate trump (Brisca) suit.

rules.objective: To win, a player or team must earn more card points than the opponent(s). The deck has 120 points in total; the first side to exceed 60 points wins the deal. If both sides tie at 60, the side with more cards wins.
rules.gameplay: Lead any card (no follow-suit obligation). Opponent plays any card. Highest Brisca (trump) wins. If no trump played, highest of led suit wins. Winner draws first from stock; loser draws second. Winner leads next trick.
keyRules: Trump beats all off-suit cards regardless of rank.
Last stock card taken is the trump indicator card.

strategy.basic: Protect the Ace and Three of trumpâ€”they alone are worth 21 of the 120 points.
strategy.intermediate: Lead low worthless cards (7-2) to bait opponents into wasting Aces. Trump an opponent's Ace only if you're sure to also score significant points.
strategy.advanced: Once the stock empties, you know both hands. Calculate exactly what remains and play to prevent the opponent's Ace of trump from taking your Three of trump.
tips: The Three of Brisca (10pts) is the most underestimated cardâ€”treat it like an Ace.
Never trump a 0-point trick unless you're holding excess trump.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Ace, 3, King, Queen, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 (high to low)
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump beats any non-trump; no overtrump obligation.

edgeCases.text: 60-60 tie: side with most cards wins.
Turned trump card may be exchanged for 7 of same suit (or 2 if turned card is 7 or lower) by holder who has won at least one trick, before last stock card is drawn.
Team holding three highest trumps may claim remaining tricks without playing them (optional variant).

customActions.description: Deal three cards to each player. Place the remainder face-down as stock and turn the top card face up beside it; that card's suit is trump (Brisca).
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; performed once at game start.

customActions.description: Play one card from hand to the current trick. No follow-suit obligation. Highest trump wins; if no trump played, highest card of the led suit wins.
customActions.constraints: Must have at least one card in hand; one card per turn.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 40-card deck: four suits (typically Spanish: coins, cups, swords, batons) with ten ranks each (ace, two through seven, plus face cards). No jokers; used for Brisca (Spanish trick-taking game) where the turned card sets trump.
engine.suitDescription: Four suits (Spanish: oros, copas, espadas, bastos). Trump is the suit of the card turned after the deal; it outranks the other three suits. Follow suit when able; each suit has ten cards. Point values: three 10, ace 11, king 4, queen 3, jack 2.
engine.rankDescription: Ten ranks per suit in Spanish order (ace, two through seven, then face cards). In Brisca the three is often the highest point card (10 points); ace 11, king 4, queen 3, jack 2, others zero. Trick order follows the 40-card pack.
